t: Paris began as a settlement of the Gallic Parisii on the Seine, became the Roman town of Lutetia after 52 BCE, and was made capital by Clovis I in 508.

The Capetian kings built it up from the 12th century into the political, religious and learning centre of France, with Notre-Dame, the Louvre and the University, and in 1328 it was the most populous city in Europe.
From the Revolution of 1789 through Haussmann's rebuilding, the siege and Commune of 1870–71 and the occupation of 1940–44, Paris was repeatedly the scene of upheaval and violence.
dyk: In September 1914, about 600 Paris taxis carried 6,000 soldiers to the front at the First Battle of the Marne, each taking five men, and the task was done within twenty-four hours.
ev: The Parisii are defeated by a Roman army under Titus Labienus, and the Romans build Lutetia
Clovis I makes Paris his capital
Construction of the cathedral of Notre-Dame begins
The plague of 1348–1349 kills forty to fifty thousand Parisians, a quarter of the population
The St Bartholomew's Day massacre kills about three thousand Protestants in Paris
A crowd storms the Bastille on 14 July and Paris becomes the stage of the Revolution
The Commune is crushed in the Bloody Week
The city is liberated on 25 August after four years of German occupation

f.founded: Settled by the Gallic Parisii between 250 and 225 BCE, with traces of earlier occupation from about 8000 BCE; the Romans built the town of Lutetia after their conquest of 52 BCE
f.where: On the Seine, with the Île de la Cité at its heart, in the Île-de-France region of northern France
f.known: the Parisii and Roman Lutetia; Notre-Dame and the Gothic style; the University of Paris; the French Revolution; Haussmann's rebuilding; the siege and Commune of 1870–71; the occupation of 1940–44; its museums and artists
f.today: Paris is the capital and largest city of France, where the president and both houses of Parliament sit.
